title: Exceptions from invalid conversion and casting
answer: There is no single exception for every kind of Java conversion. An invalid reference-type cast can throw `ClassCastException` at runtime, for example casting a `String` object to `Integer`. Converting malformed numeric text with APIs such as `Integer.parseInt` throws `NumberFormatException`. Primitive numeric casts such as `double` to `int` or `int` to `byte` normally do not throw merely because information is lost; they follow Java's numeric-conversion rules. Other conversion-related operations can fail differently, so the correct exception depends on the conversion being performed.
